sections.text: Introduction

The Consort pH meter P107 measures the 
 pH in a solution. pH is a measure of relative acidity or alkalinity of water; 
 so, it is a most important factor influencing scaleforming and corrosion 
 tendencies.

The first draft initiated and tested by chem. 
 Houssam Mohamed Mesbash, reviewed by general manager chem: Mohamed Ahmed 
 Farag, revised by EDEPC quality control chemist Wael A. Tantawy, 
 approved by eng.Fawzi Sobhee Esmail: head sector of Abu Sultan PS,
 and 
 certified by accountant Mahmoud Mohamed Soliman; general director of Admin.& 
 Financial quality control, and supervisor of EDEPC inspection & quality 
 control Head Sector.

pH 
measurement

A pH measurement is always relative which makes 
it necessary to use standards. Each time the pH meter is switched on or 
electrodes are changed, the instrument should be standardized with 2 buffers 
differing from each other by at least 2 units, in order to compensate for:

Zero point: Each electrode has its own specific pH value, corresponding to the zero 
potential point (ISO-pH). This specific pH value can differ from its theoretical 
zero point (e.g. 7 pH) by a few tenths of a pH.

Slope: A good 
electrode follows the Nernst Equation within 90 to 100 %. If the slope lies outside these limits, the 
electrode becomes slow & may not be optimal for most application.
Select the pH mode.

Adjust the temperature 
compensation to the temperature of the solution.

After rinsing the 
electrode with distilled water, immerse them in a buffer solution of pH as close 
as possible to the ISO-pH of the electrode (e.g. 6.87 pH).

Standardize to the pH of 
the buffer with the CALIBRATION button.

After rinsing the 
electrode with distilled water. Immerse them in a second buffer solution of pH 
close to the pH to be measured (e.g. 4.01 pH).

Standardize to the pH of 
the buffer with the SLOPE button.

After rinsing the electrode with 
distilled water, immerse them in the solution to be measured and read the 
display.

Rinse the electrode 
always with distilled water after use and store them in a 3.5 M KCl solution.
Note: Stirring 
the solution during the measurements promotes the homogeneity and is therefore 
always recommended.

sections.text: Directives
Maintenance of the CONSORT pH Meter P107

The 
normal operating temperature should be between 0Cand 
40C. 
Never store the instruments in a room with high humidity or at very low 
temperatures (condensation of water).
Electrode Maintenance

pH Electrode: A pH electrode is active and stable 
only after wetting. For this purpose it must be immersed for at least 10 hours 
in a 3.5 M KCl solution. During short interruptions (e.g. storage) the electrode 
should be immersed in a 3.5 M KCl solution. In doing this it is always kept 
ready for use. When the interruption is longer than month, refill the closing 
cap with 3.5 M KCl and plug it on the electrode tip in order to protect the glass 
bulb.

A polluted electrode may be cleaned with a soft 
detergent or 0.1 M HCl. Greasy substances may be removed with acetone or alcohol [never do this with plastic electrode]. If the electrode is polluted by 
proteinaceous materials (such as blood). It should stand in a pepsin solution 
overnight and then be cleaned before use.

The pH electrode wears away by being used. If 
the electrode tends to respond slower and calibration becomes difficult, even 
after cleaning, it should be replaced by a new one.

Metal electrodes (pt, Ag, Au): Metal electrodes 
are always ready for use. During short interruptions they are immersed in 
distilled water. They should be cleaned regularly:

Silver electrodes are immersed in a 
concentrated ammonia solution during one hour.

Platinum or gold electrodes are immersed in 
concentrated nitric acid during one hour.
